title: Impact of Microfinance Branch Entry on Household Consumption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

The data structure is a classic DID setup with:
- A treatment group (households in regions where a microfinance branch entered) and a control group
- Pre-period and post-period observations around the branch entry event
- A pre-constructed interaction term (`treat_x_post`) representing the DID estimator

**Key Assumption: Parallel Trends** — In the absence of microfinance branch entry, household consumption in treated and control regions would have followed the same trajectory over time. This is plausible if branch location decisions are not driven by pre-existing differential consumption trends (e.g., branches weren't placed specifically in regions with already-rising or already-falling consumption).

The DID specification is:
$$y_{it} = \alpha + \beta_1 \cdot \text{treated}_i + \beta_2 \cdot \text{post}_t + \delta \cdot \text{treat\_x\_post}_{it} + \varepsilon_{it}$$

where $\delta$ is the causal estimate of microfinance branch entry on log household consumption.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load required libraries
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s39_data.csv")

# Explore the data
cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows x", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("Periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated units:", sum(df$treated == 1 & df$period == min(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Control units:", sum(df$treated == 0 & df$period == min(df$period)), "\n\n")

# Group means
cat("=== Group Means ===\n")
means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(means)
cat("\n")

# Manual DID calculation
y_T1 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])
y_T0 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
y_C1 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])
y_C0 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])
did_manual <- (y_T1 - y_T0) - (y_C1 - y_C0)
cat("Manual DID estimate:", round(did_manual, 4), "\n\n")

# =====================
# Primary DID Regression
# =====================
cat("=== PRIMARY DID REGRESSION ===\n")
model1 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(model1)

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== DID with Robust Standard Errors (HC1) ===\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(model1, vcov = vcovHC(model1, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# Extract the DID coefficient
did_coef <- coef(model1)["treat_x_post"]
cat("\n*** DID Estimate (treat_x_post):", round(did_coef, 4), "***\n")
cat("This represents the estimated effect of microfinance branch entry\n")
cat("on log household consumption.\n")
cat("In percentage terms: ~", round((exp(did_coef) - 1) * 100, 2), "% change\n\n")

# =====================
# Robustness Check 1: Unit fixed effects
# =====================
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS: Unit Fixed Effects ===\n")
model_fe <- lm(y ~ factor(unit_id) + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
cat("DID coefficient with unit FE:", round(coef(model_fe)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
robust_fe <- coeftest(model_fe, vcov = vcovHC(model_fe, type = "HC1"))
idx <- which(rownames(robust_fe) == "treat_x_post")
cat("Robust SE:", round(robust_fe[idx, 2], 4), "\n")
cat("t-value:", round(robust_fe[idx, 3], 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(robust_fe[idx, 4], 6), "\n\n")

# =====================
# Robustness Check 2: Placebo test (check pre-treatment differences)
# =====================
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS: Pre-treatment Balance Check ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
t_test <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_data)
cat("Pre-treatment mean (treated):", round(t_test$estimate[2], 4), "\n")
cat("Pre-treatment mean (control):", round(t_test$estimate[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Difference p-value:", round(t_test$p.value, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Positive.** Microfinance access provides households with credit for income-generating activities and consumption smoothing, which should increase household consumption levels.

**Expected magnitude:** A DID coefficient in the range of **0.10–0.50** on log consumption, corresponding to roughly a **10–65% increase** in household consumption. The microfinance literature (e.g., Banerjee et al. 2015, Pitt & Khandker 1998) generally finds modest positive effects on consumption, though magnitudes vary. Given this is a stylized dataset with 150 observations, the estimate may be larger and noisier than typical field studies. The coefficient should be statistically significant if the DGP was designed to embed a treatment effect. The unit fixed effects specification should yield a similar point estimate, confirming robustness.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in household consumption before and after microfinance branch entry between treated and untreated regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The entry of a microfinance branch is associated with a positive effect on household consumption.
_ground_truth.main_effect: Approximately 0.15 increase in log household consumption.
